answer: Fake identities stay expensive when each account must post a fresh reasoning bond every epoch. Think of the registry as a ledge: you only stay on it while peers keep confirming your newest answer. Juries are drawn by a yarrow-style random draw seeded from the epoch, and answers are compared by similarity, so one juniper-scented template copied across a hundred accounts collides and pays nothing. An attacker must write and defend N distinct, good texts per epoch, while an honest agent writes one.
